llmAnalysis.summary: Plugin is a local-first clock/calendar with confined IPC and helper-script execution; static flags are largely benign. Resolved URLs point to bundled Panel.qml and fixed allow-list scripts, IPC exposes only no-arg UI verbs, and openUrlExternally is user-click-gated to https meeting links.
llmAnalysis.whatItDoes: Plugin replaces the bar clock with a configurable date/time label and calendar popup. The popup shows a 6-week month grid with ISO weeks, year/life progress bars, and a per-day agenda synced via local Caldir ICS cache with optional Google pull/push via OAuth (direct or hosted). Users can create/edit recurring local events, get 5-min reminders, and JOIN meeting links directly.

    BarWidget->>Panel: Loader source Qt.resolvedUrl("Panel.qml") / toggle()
    Panel->>Helper: helperPath("calendar-cache-read") via Process.command

    Panel->>Helper: calendar-create / calendar-mutate / calendar-push
    Helper->>Google: authenticated sync (OAuth)
    User->>Panel: click JOIN
    Panel->>Browser: Qt.openUrlExternally(meetingLinks[0])

findings.reasoning: Static local QML import via Loader source: Qt.resolvedUrl("Panel.qml") loads bundled panel UI, never used as Process command or external path; no user input.
findings.executableContext: Not an executable — internal QML component load only, no Process execution.

findings.reasoning: IpcHandler target "omarchy-google-calendar-clock" exposes 10 fixed-arity no-arg verbs (open/close/toggle/cycleFormat/refreshCalendar/calendarStatus); no payload parsing or validation needed, cannot inject args or execute arbitrary commands. Worst is local unprivileged UI spam.
findings.relatedCode: IpcHandler { target: "omarchy-google-calendar-clock"; function refresh():void; function cycleFormat():void; function calendarStatus():string { return panelLoader.item.calendarStatus() } } BarWidget.qml:129-145
findings.executableContext: Indirect: refreshCalendar() triggers calendar-cache-read via helperPath, but path is hardcoded allow-list, not IPC-controllable.

findings.reasoning: Panel declares ipcTarget with manageIpc:false — actual handler lives in BarWidget.qml:129; same low-risk no-arg verbs, no deserialization of external payload, intentionally disabled on panel side.
findings.relatedCode: Panel { ipcTarget: "omarchy-google-calendar-clock" manageIpc: false } Panel.qml:22-24; BarWidget handles IPC
findings.executableContext: No direct executable; duplicate declaration of same IPC target.

findings.reasoning: helperPath() does Qt.resolvedUrl("scripts/"+name) but all callers pass hardcoded literals (calendar-cache-read, calendar-pull/push, calendar-create/mutate, etc.); name never from settings/IPC/event data, so no traversal/injection despite being used as Process.command[0].

findings.executableContext: Resolves bundled Caldir wrapper scripts (calendar-* , setup/uninstall) that sync local ICS with Google. Args are sanitized: dates via Model.keyForDate, time HH:MM regex, repeat count 2-999, Util.shellQuote for terminal flows; scripts run as user with fixed argv array, not shell.

findings.reasoning: User-gated JOIN button calls Qt.openUrlExternally(agendaEvent.meetingLinks[0]) only on explicit click; meetingLinks are https?:// URLs extracted via CalendarModel.eventMeetingLinks from conference_url/location/description, priorizing meet.google.com/zoom.us etc; no auto-open and not IPC-triggerable.
